newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia Development Fund sets loans criteria - agency.
newsitem.headline: Serbia Development Fund sets loans criteria - agency.

text.p: The Serbian Development Fund Board of Directors determined on Tuesday conditions for extending credits from funds raised through a sale of Serbia's telecommunciations company Telekom Srbije.

It has drafted a programme for granting loans to firms for export projects which was submitted to the Serbian government for approval and will allocate first loans this week, state news agency Tanjug reported.

The Serbian Development Fund is the sole recipient of nearly one billion dollars which Serbia raised through the sale of a 49 percent stake in Telekom Srbija earlier this month to Italy's Stet and Greece's OTE.
Under the agreement 80 percent of the sum was to be paid immediately and the rest in January 1988.
All firms which have profitable programmes, export deals or fulfill other conditions set by the Fund qualify for the credits, the Fund was quoted as saying.
But the Fund fell short from detailing conditions under which companies' qualify for part of the Telekom's money.
Loans will be allocated to firms from the sector of industry, metal complex, agriculture, textile production, leather and footwear industry, shipbuilding and other sectors.
The Fund will also finance construction of regional roads and highways and railway modernisation.

It said the funds earmarked for export projects must be used solely for kick-starting production in firms whose products have a secured export market or which can ensure real employment and quality production.
The Fund demands firm guarantees that the credits will be used for the set purpose and repaid at the set time under determined conditions.
Credits will be extended under extremely favourable conditions with a four percent interest rate and banks providing 0.002 percent funds as a guarantee.

"The programme aims at fully supporting the Serbian government's economic policy which is directed at increasing production and GDP while keeping dinar and price stability and raising wages and the standard of living," The Fund said.
